name: Should I choose MDF or solid wood for interior trim and molding?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose MDF or solid wood for interior trim and molding?

acceptedAnswer.text: MDF is an engineered product that provides a smooth, uniform surface ideal for painted trim, while solid wood offers natural grain suitable for staining or clear-coating. MDF does not warp easily and costs less, but it swells when exposed to persistent moisture, making it less suitable for high-humidity areas or baseboards near damp floors unless thoroughly sealed. Solid wood withstands minor impact better and holds detailed edge profiles sharply, though it expands and contracts with indoor humidity changes. Choosing between them depends on whether you intend to paint or stain the trim and the moisture levels of the room.
acceptedAnswer.description: MDF is cost-effective and provides a smooth finish for paint, while solid wood is durable, handles moisture better, and can be stained to display natural grain.
